questions.stem: What is the condition for a pair of linear equations to have a unique solution?
choices: The lines intersect at a point.
The lines have the same slope but different intercepts.
The lines have the same slope and same intercepts.
questions.solution: The correct answer is that the lines intersect at a point. This is because when two lines intersect, there is exactly one point that satisfies both equations, resulting in a unique solution. The other options are incorrect: parallel lines have no solution, coinciding lines have infinitely many solutions, and perpendicular lines are not a condition for a unique solution.

hi.stem: एक रैखिक समीकरण युग्म के एक अद्वितीय हल के लिए क्या शर्त है?

रेखाएँ समान ढलान और समान अंतःखंड रखती हैं।
hi.solution: सही उत्तर यह है कि रेखाएँ एक बिंदु पर प्रतिच्छेद करती हैं। इसका कारण यह है कि जब दो रेखाएँ प्रतिच्छेद करती हैं, तो दोनों समीकरणों को संतुष्ट करने वाला एक बिंदु होता है, जिसके कारण एक अद्वितीय हल प्राप्त होता है। अन्य विकल्प गलत हैं: समांतर रेखाओं के कोई हल नहीं होते, संपाती रेखाओं के अनंत हल होते हैं और लंबवत रेखाएँ अद्वितीय हल के लिए एक शर्त नहीं हैं।

questions.stem: What type of solution does a pair of linear equations have if their lines are parallel?
questions.solution: If the lines represented by a pair of linear equations are parallel, they never intersect, which means there is no solution to the equations. This is known as an inconsistent pair of equations. The other options are incorrect because they describe situations where the lines intersect or coincide, which are not the case for parallel lines.

questions.stem: If the lines represented by a pair of linear equations are coincident, what can be said about the solution of the equations?

questions.stem: If the pair of equations 2x + 3y = 5 and 4x + 6y = 10 is solved algebraically, what will be the nature of the solution?
questions.solution: The second equation is a multiple of the first equation, meaning they represent the same line. This results in infinitely many solutions. The other options either describe inconsistency or a unique solution, which is not the case here.

questions.stem: Given the pair of equations 6x – 3y + 10 = 0 and 2x – y + 9 = 0, what is the relationship between the lines they represent?
questions.solution: The given pair of equations is 6x – 3y + 10 = 0 and 2x – y + 9 = 0. By comparing the ratios of their coefficients, we find that the lines are parallel. This means they have no solution and are inconsistent. The other options are incorrect because intersecting lines would have a unique solution, coincident lines would have infinitely many solutions, and lines cannot intersect at two points.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a correct step in the elimination method for solving linear equations?
choices: Multiply both equations by the same constant to eliminate one variable.
Add the two equations directly to eliminate one variable.
Subtract one equation from the other without adjusting coefficients.

questions.stem: A pair of linear equations has no solution. Which of the following must be true about the lines representing these equations?
questions.solution: If a pair of linear equations has no solution, the lines representing them must be parallel. This is because parallel lines never intersect.
